newsitem.title: USA: White House has no comment on Tyson replacement.
newsitem.headline: White House has no comment on Tyson replacement.

text.p: A White House spokeman on Thursday declined comment on a published report that President Bill Clinton is considering naming two people to take over Laura Tyson's job as chair of the National Economic Council.

The Wall Street Journal on Thursday reported that Clinton was leaning toward naming Tyson's current deputy Gene Sperling and Daniel Tarullo, the White House "sherpa" who prepares Group of Seven summit meetings, to share the job.
The National Economic Council was created by Clinton to coordinate the administration's economic policy. Tyson is leaving to teach at the University of California at Berkeley.
